para: Each subtitle is constructed from a format string. A variety of variables are available that reflect aspects of the track. The format string is similar to C++ std::format and Python f-strings, but must always contain the variable name.

Variables are accessed by using a named field, which are curly braces containing the variable name. An optional format specification can be provided for each field. The format specification controls aspects such as the total width (number of characters), the alignment within the field width, decimal digits shown, and so on.

The format specification depends on the variable type, shown in the table below. If the format specification is not appropriate for the type, an error such as "subrip: format error for hour: Invalid presentation type for integer" will be shown.

Vertical velocity. Assumed to be meters-per-second by default.
Type "\n" in the format string to insert a newline and produce multi-line subtitles.

para: The default format string is {speed:4.1f} m/s {altitude:4.0f} m\n{hour:02d}:{minute:02d}:{second:02d} Lat={latitude:.5f} Lon={longitude:.5f}. A possible format for a bicycle video is {speed:<4.1f} m/s{heartrate:5.0f} bpm\n{altitude:<6.1f} m{cadence:5.0f} rpm.
